guardrails: Association is not proof of individual causation.
Bidirectional relationships are common between health, mental health, work, housing and relationships.
Pain, sleep, medications, endocrine/neurological factors, poverty, discrimination and access can confound observed relationships.
ACE counts are not destiny and do not capture the full meaning, severity or context of adversity.
A diagnosis or event must not be used to predict one person's prognosis without person-specific evidence.
The same diagnosis can be mild, episodic, severe, progressive, stable or profoundly disabling in different people.
The same life event can feel traumatic, relieving, mixed, manageable or life-changing depending on context.
Compare with the person's own baseline and priorities.
Preserve autonomy and ask which supports are wanted.
Record strengths and retained abilities as carefully as losses and limitations.
